findings.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:133 — if (dateOverrideExist) return true` short-circuits before the `busy.every` check, so any slot inside a date-override window is shown as available even if an existing booking, calendar event, or buffer overlaps it (double-booking exposure for fixed and round-robin hosts).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:106 — dateOverrides.find` returns "outside override" as soon as the first same-day range misses, so when a date override has multiple ranges (e.g. 9-10 and 14-15), slots in the second and later ranges get rejected.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:139 — The working-hours check rejects a slot if it falls outside ANY same-weekday entry rather than ALL of them, so split schedules (lunch breaks) and hours that getWorkingHours splits across UTC midnight (e.g. US Pacific/Sydney) lose most or all slots.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:110 — Override applicability is keyed on the UTC calendar date of the override start, so an override whose UTC range crosses midnight wipes the organizer's regular hours on the adjacent UTC day, and override slots after UTC midnight fall through to working-hours and get rejected.

packages/lib/slots.ts:218 — Override start/end are turned into invitee minutes-of-day with `.hour()*60+.minute()`, which wraps at midnight (e.g. IST 09:00-11:00 viewed from New York gives start=1410, end=90), so buildSlots drops the range as invalid and the invitee sees no slots on that override day.

packages/lib/slots.ts:212 — Overrides are now converted using the offsets on the override date, but buildSlots still adds `organizerDSTDiff - inviteeDSTDiff` (based on today's offset), so DST gets corrected twice and overrides in the other DST season shift by 1h and lose their edge slot.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:114 — The zero-length (unavailable-all-day) override check compares two Dayjs objects with `===`, which is always false, so a slot starting exactly at the override instant falls through to `dateOverrideExist` and returns available.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:142 — end` is computed from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, so the working-hours check never catches a slot that runs past the end of working hours.

packages/lib/slots.ts:207 — The active-override filter compares the fake-UTC override start to the invitee's day while checkIfIsAvailable matches on the real UTC date, so the invitee-supplied `timeZone` decides which day an "unavailable" override blocks (e.g. a Sydney organizer's blocked day still shows afternoon slots to New York invitees).

apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:799 — The new assertion only covers IST vs Dhaka (30-minute delta, no DST, no midnight crossing, no booking inside the override), and `toHaveTimeSlots` iterates the actual slots with `.every`, so it passes on a subset and would not catch the busy-bypass or midnight-wrap regressions.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:110 — dayjs(date.start).add(...)` is in local mode and formats in the server's local time zone while `slotStartTime` formats in UTC, so the same-day match breaks on any server whose TZ is not UTC.

packages/lib/slots.ts:212 — override.timeZone` is optional, and `.tz(undefined)` falls back to the default or server time zone, so any getSlots caller that omits it silently gets a wrong organizer offset; the offsets are also taken at the fake-UTC instant, which is wrong by up to an hour near DST transitions.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:133 — if (dateOverrideExist) return true` returns before the `busy.every` check, so existing bookings and calendar busy times are ignored on any day that has a date override, which allows double booking.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:106 — dateOverrides.find` rejects the slot if it falls outside ANY override range on that date, so a day with several override ranges (e.g. 9-12 and 14-17) rejects every slot.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:110 — The override day is matched on the UTC date of the converted start, not the organizer's calendar day: an early or late override (e.g. 02:00 in +6 = previous-day UTC) blocks the organizer's whole adjacent day, and override slots past UTC midnight skip the override check.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:110 — dayjs(date.start)...format("YYYY MM DD")` formats in the server's local time zone while `slotStartTime` formats in UTC, so override date matching depends on the server's TZ.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:114 — ===` between two separately built dayjs objects is always false, so the zero-length ("unavailable all day") override branch is dead code and a slot starting exactly at that instant passes.
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:123 — The override end check uses `slotStartTime.isAfter(end)`, so a slot that starts exactly at the override end or runs past it is treated as available.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:139 — workingHours.find` rejects the slot if it falls outside ANY entry for that weekday, so split shifts or ranges that getWorkingHours splits at UTC midnight (e.g. an organizer in a UTC-8 zone) reject every slot.
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:142 — end` is computed from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, so slots that run past the end of working hours are never rejected.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:140 — The working-hours check compares raw UTC minutes built with the organizer's current offset, with no DST adjustment for the slot's date (getSlots/buildSlots do adjust), so valid first-hour slots are rejected in the other DST season.

packages/lib/slots.ts:214 — Override times are now converted with the offset at the override's date, but buildSlots still adds organizerDSTDiff-inviteeDSTDiff, so DST is corrected twice (e.g. a London override for a UTC invitee shifts by 1h when the override date and today are in different DST seasons).

packages/lib/slots.ts:219 — hour*60+minute` after shifting by the offset wraps at midnight: an override that crosses the invitee's day boundary gets endTime < startTime, and buildSlots silently drops it (`start >= end`).

packages/lib/slots.ts:214 — activeOverrides` still picks the invitee day using the unshifted wall-clock start, so after the offset is applied the override can show up on the wrong invitee day while the correct day keeps its normal working hours.
packages/lib/slots.ts:212 — override.timeZone` is optional and there is no fallback to `organizerTimeZone`, so `.tz(undefined)` silently uses the server's local time zone.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:107 — The organizer offset is computed at the fake-UTC wall-clock instant, not at the real instant, so overrides within a few hours of a DST transition are shifted by an hour.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:105 — checkIfIsAvailable now linearly scans the host's full dateOverrides list on every slot x host call (including slots on days with no override, since find only short-circuits on exclusion), doing a dayjs.tz conversion plus ~6 dayjs constructions and two format() calls per override per iteration, so getSchedule cost grows as slots x hosts x overrides (e.g. ~1000 monthly slots x 10 RR hosts x 20-50 overrides = 200k-500k tz conversions per request); precompute a per-user map of organizer-local date key -> override window once before the slot loops and do an O(1) lookup per slot

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:133 — No test puts a booking or calendar busy time inside a date-override window, and the new `if (dateOverrideExist) return true` returns before `busy.every`, so bookings on override days are silently ignored.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:139 — The working-hours branch is only exercised by the single-range IST fixture (04:00-12:30 UTC); no test covers split-day schedules or hours that cross UTC midnight, where `.find` rejects any slot outside *any* same-day entry.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:106 — No test covers multiple date-override ranges on the same date; `.find` returns true (reject) for a slot inside the second range because it lies after the first range's end.

packages/lib/slots.ts:218 — getSlots offset math has no unit tests, and the only new case is an invitee 30 min east of the organizer; an invitee west of the organizer, where the override crosses invitee midnight, is untested, and hour()/minute() wraps to endTime<startTime, which buildSlots drops.

apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:788 — The new assertion only reaches checkIfIsAvailable's accept path: in a single-user event getSlots already emits only in-override slots, so the new "slot outside override -> false" rejection branch is never exercised.
apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:56 — The toHaveTimeSlots matcher iterates only the actual slots, so the new assertion passes when trailing expected slots are missing (e.g. 11:30Z dropped).
packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:114 — The zero-length (day off) override check compares two Dayjs objects with `===` (always false), and no test covers a day-off override.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:142 — The working-hours `end` is computed from slotStartTime (same as `start`), so a slot that runs past end-of-hours passes; no test covers a slot straddling the working-hours boundary.

packages/lib/slots.ts:212 — Both test zones (Asia/Kolkata, Asia/Dhaka) are fixed-offset with no DST, so the new organizer/invitee utcOffset math combined with buildSlots' DST adjustment is untested on DST-transition days.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:517 — No test covers collective or round-robin hosts in different time zones with date overrides, even though the change adds per-host `timeZone` to overrides and per-host organizerTimeZone to checkIfIsAvailable.
apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:792 — The Dhaka (+6:00) query reuses the IST-midnight window (18:30Z), so it does not cover the invitee's actual full day.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:133 — if (dateOverrideExist) return true` short-circuits before the `busy.every` check, so any slot inside a date-override window is shown as available even if an existing booking, calendar event, or buffer overlaps it (double-booking exposure for fixed and round-robin hosts).

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts), the newly added logic returns early: after determining a matching date override day, it does `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` before reaching the final `return busy.every(...)` overlap check. That means any slot on a day with a date override is marked available (unless it hit the earlier `return false` path for being outside the override window), even if `busy` contains an overlapping booking/calendar event/buffer. The diff clearly introduces this short-circuit and thus can expose double-booking.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:106 — dateOverrides.find` returns "outside override" as soon as the first same-day range misses, so when a date override has multiple ranges (e.g. 9-10 and 14-15), slots in the second and later ranges get rejected.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` the code uses `dateOverrides.find(...)` to detect that a slot is *outside* an override on the same day and then immediately returns `false` ("slot is not within the date override"). Because the callback returns `true` when `slotStartTime` is after `date.end` (or `slotEndTime` is before/at `date.start`), a slot that belongs to a *later* override range on the same day will be rejected as soon as it is outside the *first* same-day override range encountered (e.g., outside 09:00–10:00, even if inside 14:00–15:00). This matches the finding and is directly implied by the `find` short-circuit behavior in the diff around the new date override logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:139 — The working-hours check rejects a slot if it falls outside ANY same-weekday entry rather than ALL of them, so split schedules (lunch breaks) and hours that getWorkingHours splits across UTC midnight (e.g. US Pacific/Sydney) lose most or all slots.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:110 — Override applicability is keyed on the UTC calendar date of the override start, so an override whose UTC range crosses midnight wipes the organizer's regular hours on the adjacent UTC day, and override slots after UTC midnight fall through to working-hours and get rejected.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, override applicability is effectively gated by a same-day check: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset,"minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") === slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")`. Since `slotStartTime` is UTC (`time.utc()`), an override whose (adjusted) range crosses UTC midnight will only be considered (`dateOverrideExist = true`) for slots on the UTC calendar date matching the override *start*. Slots after UTC midnight won’t match this date condition, so `dateOverrideExist` remains false and the code falls through to the working-hours filter, which can reject those slots even though they are within the override range. This matches the finding’s described failure mode.

If the timezone offset adjustment crosses midnight, the computed minutes-of-day will wrap (e.g., end becomes smaller than start), producing an override range where `startTime > endTime`. The diff does not show any handling for cross-midnight ranges, so this can lead to overrides being treated as invalid/ignored downstream.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:110 — dayjs(date.start).add(...)` is in local mode and formats in the server's local time zone while `slotStartTime` formats in UTC, so the same-day match breaks on any server whose TZ is not UTC.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the date-override day match compares `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` (constructed in server-local mode because `dayjs(date.start)` is not `.utc()`/`.tz()`) against `slotStartTime.format(...)` where `slotStartTime = time.utc()` (UTC mode). This mixed timezone basis can shift the formatted day depending on the server's local TZ, causing incorrect same-day matching and override application on non-UTC servers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/slots.ts:212 — override.timeZone` is optional, and `.tz(undefined)` falls back to the default or server time zone, so any getSlots caller that omits it silently gets a wrong organizer offset; the offsets are also taken at the fake-UTC instant, which is wrong by up to an hour near DST transitions.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the new logic calls `dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()` without guarding `override.timeZone` (lines around the modified block). The diff also makes `timeZone?: string` optional in `packages/types/schedule.d.ts`, so from the diff alone it’s possible for `activeOverrides` entries to omit `timeZone`, which would make `.tz(undefined)` fall back to a default timezone and compute an incorrect organizer offset. This would silently shift override start/end minutes incorrectly for any caller that doesn’t populate `timeZone`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:133 — if (dateOverrideExist) return true` returns before the `busy.every` check, so existing bookings and calendar busy times are ignored on any day that has a date override, which allows double booking.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, after determining a date override exists for the slot day, the code does `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` (added around the new override logic). This returns before the final `return busy.every(...)` block, so calendar `busy` intervals (and thus existing bookings/busy times) are not checked on any day where a date override exists and the slot is within that override window. That can incorrectly mark a slot as available even if `busy` contains a conflicting interval, enabling double-booking.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:106 — dateOverrides.find` rejects the slot if it falls outside ANY override range on that date, so a day with several override ranges (e.g. 9-12 and 14-17) rejects every slot.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` the `dateOverrides.find(...)` callback returns `true` when the slot is *outside* an override window (e.g., `slotEndTime <= override.start` or `slotStartTime > override.end`). Because it iterates all overrides on the same day, a slot that is inside one override range but outside another (e.g. inside 9–12 but before 14–17) will cause `.find` to succeed on the other range and the function returns `false` (“slot is not within the date override”). This matches the finding: multiple override ranges on the same day can lead to rejecting otherwise valid slots.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:110 — The override day is matched on the UTC date of the converted start, not the organizer's calendar day: an early or late override (e.g. 02:00 in +6 = previous-day UTC) blocks the organizer's whole adjacent day, and override slots past UTC midnight skip the override check.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` the override is considered applicable only when `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset,"minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") === slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")`, where `slotStartTime` is forced to UTC (`time.utc()`). The code derives `utcOffset` from `organizerTimeZone` but then still compares *UTC-formatted* dates, so overrides near local midnight (e.g. 02:00 at +6) can fall on the previous/next UTC date and be matched against the wrong day, causing slots on the organizer’s intended day to skip/incorrectly apply the override. This matches the finding’s described adjacent-day/UTC-midnight failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:110 — dayjs(date.start)...format("YYYY MM DD")` formats in the server's local time zone while `slotStartTime` formats in UTC, so override date matching depends on the server's TZ.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, `slotStartTime` is explicitly converted to UTC (`const slotStartTime = time.utc()`), and then formatted. But the override side uses `dayjs(date.start)` (no `.utc()` / `.tz()`), so its `.format("YYYY MM DD")` is based on the server/local timezone. Although an offset is added, the base moment is still created in local time, so the day-comparison against a UTC-formatted `slotStartTime` can vary depending on the server TZ. This matches the finding and is a correctness issue in the new override-matching logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:114 — ===` between two separately built dayjs objects is always false, so the zero-length ("unavailable all day") override branch is dead code and a slot starting exactly at that instant passes.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new date-override logic compares two separately constructed Dayjs instances with `===`: `dayjs(date.start).add(... ) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)`. This will virtually always be false because it compares object identity, so the intended “start equals end” (zero-length override) branch never triggers. As a result, when `date.start` and `date.end` represent the same instant, the code falls through and (since `dateOverrideExist` becomes true) returns `true`, allowing slots that should be rejected by that override.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:123 — The override end check uses `slotStartTime.isAfter(end)`, so a slot that starts exactly at the override end or runs past it is treated as available.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the date-override exclusion logic only flags a slot as outside the override when `slotStartTime.isAfter(dayjs(date.end)... )`. If a slot starts exactly at the override end, `isAfter` is false, and there is also no check that `slotEndTime` exceeds the override end. Because `dateOverrideExist` is set to true for that day, the function then returns `true` (available) even though the slot starts at (or can extend past) the override end.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:139 — workingHours.find` rejects the slot if it falls outside ANY entry for that weekday, so split shifts or ranges that getWorkingHours splits at UTC midnight (e.g. an organizer in a UTC-8 zone) reject every slot.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new working-hours gate uses `workingHours.find(...)` and returns `false` (rejects) if it finds *any* `workingHour` for that weekday where `start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime` (lines shown around the new block). With multiple `WorkingHours` entries for the same day (e.g., split shifts), a slot that is valid in one range will still be rejected as soon as it is outside another range, because `find` only needs one mismatch to trigger rejection. This matches the finding’s core claim. (Also, `end` is incorrectly computed from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, making the check even more error-prone.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:142 — end` is computed from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, so slots that run past the end of working hours are never rejected.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:140 — The working-hours check compares raw UTC minutes built with the organizer's current offset, with no DST adjustment for the slot's date (getSlots/buildSlots do adjust), so valid first-hour slots are rejected in the other DST season.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` the working-hours check uses `slotStartTime = time.utc()` and then computes minutes via `slotStartTime.hour()/minute()`. It does not apply the organizer’s offset (current or otherwise) or any DST-specific adjustment there. So the finding’s claim that it compares minutes “built with the organizer's current offset” is not supported by the diff. (There may be other issues in this block—e.g., `end` is set equal to `start`—but that’s not what the finding asserts.)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `packages/lib/slots.ts` changing how override `startTime`/`endTime` minutes are computed using timezone utcOffsets at the override date. However, the finding claims that `buildSlots` still applies an additional `organizerDSTDiff - inviteeDSTDiff` adjustment, causing a double DST correction. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/slots.ts:219 — hour*60+minute` after shifting by the offset wraps at midnight: an override that crosses the invitee's day boundary gets endTime < startTime, and buildSlots silently drops it (`start >= end`).

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the new override conversion computes `startTime`/`endTime` as `dayjs(...).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 + ...minute()`, which discards the date and only keeps time-of-day. If applying `offset` shifts either boundary across midnight in the invitee’s timezone, the computed minutes-since-midnight can wrap (e.g., 23:30 -> 00:30), making `endTime` numerically less than `startTime` even when the real range is valid. That creates an invalid-looking range for downstream slot building logic that expects `startTime < endTime`, matching the finding’s concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/slots.ts:214 — activeOverrides` still picks the invitee day using the unshifted wall-clock start, so after the offset is applied the override can show up on the wrong invitee day while the correct day keeps its normal working hours.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts` the override conversion now applies a minute offset (`inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset`) and then derives only `hour()`/`minute()` from `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute")`. This encodes overrides purely as minutes-within-a-day, without preserving/adjusting which calendar day the override should belong to after the offset. If the offset pushes the override across midnight for the invitee, the override’s minutes can be applied to the “current” day’s working hours even though it belongs to the adjacent invitee day, effectively leaving the correct invitee day unmodified and modifying the wrong one.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/slots.ts:212 — override.timeZone` is optional and there is no fallback to `organizerTimeZone`, so `.tz(undefined)` silently uses the server's local time zone.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the new logic unconditionally calls `dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone)` to compute `organizerUtcOffset`, but `override.timeZone` is declared optional in `packages/types/schedule.d.ts` and there is no guard/fallback in this function. While `getSchedule` now populates `timeZone` when flattening `availability.dateOverrides`, the diff does not prove all `activeOverrides` will always carry `timeZone`, so this is a concrete edge-case risk introduced by using an optional field without handling `undefined`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:107 — The organizer offset is computed at the fake-UTC wall-clock instant, not at the real instant, so overrides within a few hours of a DST transition are shifted by an hour.

adjudication.rationale: At the cited code in `checkIfIsAvailable` (around line ~107), the offset is computed as `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1`. Given `date.start` is a real `Date` instant, `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()` is derived for that real instant (including DST rules). The diff does not show it being computed from a “fake-UTC wall-clock instant.” While the new offset/math logic is indeed suspect in other ways (e.g., shifting with `add(utcOffset, 'minutes')` and even comparing Dayjs objects by `===`), the specific claim about DST shift due to computing the offset at a fake-UTC wall-clock instant is not verifiable from the diff as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:105 — checkIfIsAvailable now linearly scans the host's full dateOverrides list on every slot x host call (including slots on days with no override, since find only short-circuits on exclusion), doing a dayjs.tz conversion plus ~6 dayjs constructions and two format() calls per override per iteration, so getSchedule cost grows as slots x hosts x overrides (e.g. ~1000 monthly slots x 10 RR hosts x 20-50 overrides = 200k-500k tz conversions per request); precompute a per-user map of organizer-local date key -> override window once before the slot loops and do an O(1) lookup per slot

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts), the new logic does `dateOverrides.find((date) => { ... dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() ... dayjs(date.start)...format(...) ... })` for every slot availability check. For slots on days with no matching override, the callback still runs for every override until the end because it only returns `true` in certain exclusion cases, so it becomes O(slots × overrides) and performs multiple `dayjs` constructions and a `dayjs.tz` conversion per override per slot. This is a real, diff-grounded performance/scalability issue, not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:133 — No test puts a booking or calendar busy time inside a date-override window, and the new `if (dateOverrideExist) return true` returns before `busy.every`, so bookings on override days are silently ignored.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts), after the new date-override checks, the code does `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` before reaching the final `return busy.every(...)` block. This means that on any day where a matching date override exists, the function can return `true` without considering `busy` times (calendar busy/host bookings), effectively ignoring conflicts on override days. The added test in `getSchedule.test.ts` only checks timezone behavior and does not place a busy/booking interval inside an override window to catch this regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:139 — The working-hours branch is only exercised by the single-range IST fixture (04:00-12:30 UTC); no test covers split-day schedules or hours that cross UTC midnight, where `.find` rejects any slot outside *any* same-day entry.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new working-hours gate uses `workingHours.find(...)` and returns `false` if it finds *any* `workingHour` for the slot’s weekday where `start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime` (with `end` mistakenly computed the same as `start`). With multiple working-hour ranges on the same day (split schedules), a slot that is valid in one range but outside another range will be rejected as soon as `.find` hits the non-matching range. This is a real correctness issue in the diff, independent of the test-coverage claim in the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:106 — No test covers multiple date-override ranges on the same date; `.find` returns true (reject) for a slot inside the second range because it lies after the first range's end.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the date-override logic uses `dateOverrides.find(...)` and returns `false` (reject slot) if *any* override on the same UTC day deems the slot "outside" that specific range (e.g., `slotStartTime.isAfter(date.end)`). With multiple override ranges on the same date, a slot that is inside a later range but after an earlier range’s `end` will satisfy the earlier override’s `slotStartTime.isAfter(...)` check, causing `.find` to return truthy and the function to reject the slot. This is a correctness bug in the new override-handling logic; the added tests only cover a timezone case, not multiple ranges on one day.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/slots.ts:218 — getSlots offset math has no unit tests, and the only new case is an invitee 30 min east of the organizer; an invitee west of the organizer, where the override crosses invitee midnight, is untested, and hour()/minute() wraps to endTime<startTime, which buildSlots drops.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial timezone offset adjustment logic in `packages/lib/slots.ts` (computing `offset = inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` and then deriving `startTime`/`endTime` via `dayjs(...).utc().add(offset,"minute").hour()*60 + ...minute()`). The only added test exercises a different timezone in `getSchedule.test.ts`, but it does not cover negative offsets (invitee west of organizer) or cases where applying the offset could make the derived minutes-of-day wrap across midnight. Since the code collapses adjusted datetimes to `hour()`/`minute()` (discarding the day), an interval that crosses midnight after adjustment could yield `endTime < startTime`, an edge case that is untested in this diff. The claim that it is “the only new case is 30 min east” and that `buildSlots` drops it isn’t directly verifiable from the shown diff, but the missing targeted tests for the new offset math is a concrete review concern grounded in the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:788 — The new assertion only reaches checkIfIsAvailable's accept path: in a single-user event getSlots already emits only in-override slots, so the new "slot outside override -> false" rejection branch is never exercised.

adjudication.rationale: The added test in `apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts` only asserts a set of returned slots for the override case (a success/accept outcome). In the diff, `checkIfIsAvailable` gained new early-rejection logic for slots outside a date override / outside working hours (the `return false;` branches around the new `dateOverrides.find(...)` and `workingHours.find(...)` checks in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts`), but the new test does not explicitly assert that any candidate slot is rejected by those new branches. The finding’s specific claim that `getSlots` *already* filters to only in-override slots cannot be fully verified from the shown diff, but the broader point (new nontrivial rejection logic lacks direct test coverage) is grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:56 — The toHaveTimeSlots matcher iterates only the actual slots, so the new assertion passes when trailing expected slots are missing (e.g. 11:30Z dropped).

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows a new test assertion using `toHaveTimeSlots`, but it does not include the implementation of the `toHaveTimeSlots` matcher, so the claim that it “iterates only the actual slots” (and would therefore pass when trailing expected slots are missing) cannot be verified from this PR diff. Additionally, the finding references `apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:56`, while the added assertion appears around line ~784 in the shown diff, suggesting the report is not grounded in the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:114 — The zero-length (day off) override check compares two Dayjs objects with `===` (always false), and no test covers a day-off override.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` (around the new date override logic), the “zero-length/day off” check uses strict equality on two separately-created Dayjs instances: `if (dayjs(date.start).add(... ) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)) { ... }`. This comparison will always be false because it compares object identities rather than timestamps, so the intended zero-length override branch can never trigger. The added test in `getSchedule.test.ts` covers timezone behavior but does not exercise a zero-length/day-off override case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:142 — The working-hours `end` is computed from slotStartTime (same as `start`), so a slot that runs past end-of-hours passes; no test covers a slot straddling the working-hours boundary.

packages/lib/slots.ts:212 — Both test zones (Asia/Kolkata, Asia/Dhaka) are fixed-offset with no DST, so the new organizer/invitee utcOffset math combined with buildSlots' DST adjustment is untested on DST-transition days.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new timezone-offset reconciliation logic in `packages/lib/slots.ts` using `dayjs(...).tz(...).utcOffset()` to compute an `offset` between organizer and invitee timezones, then shifts override times by that offset. This logic is sensitive to DST because `utcOffset()` can vary by date. The newly added test in `apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts` uses a fixed `+6:00` offset timezone, which does not exercise DST-changing offsets, so DST-transition behavior of the new offset math is not covered by tests. The finding’s mention of a separate `buildSlots` DST adjustment isn’t directly verifiable from this diff, but the “untested on DST-transition days” point is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:517 — No test covers collective or round-robin hosts in different time zones with date overrides, even though the change adds per-host `timeZone` to overrides and per-host organizerTimeZone to checkIfIsAvailable.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial per-host timezone handling for date overrides: `dateOverrides` are extended with `timeZone: availability.timeZone` (getSchedule mapping) and `checkIfIsAvailable` now takes `organizerTimeZone` passed per schedule/user (`organizerTimeZone: schedule.timeZone` and `userSchedule?.timeZone` in the collective/round-robin-related branches). However, the only new test in `apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts` covers a single schedule scenario with a different invitee timezone, and the diff shows no new tests exercising collective/round-robin multi-host cases where hosts have different time zones and date overrides. Given the added per-host branching, the missing coverage is a specific, diff-grounded test gap rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts:792 — The Dhaka (+6:00) query reuses the IST-midnight window (18:30Z), so it does not cover the invitee's actual full day.

adjudication.rationale: The added test calls `getSchedule` with `timeZone: Timezones["+6:00"]` but keeps the same UTC window (`startTime` at `${plus1DateString}T18:30:00.000Z` through `${plus2DateString}T18:29:59.999Z`) and asserts identical UTC slots. A 24h window starting at 18:30Z corresponds to midnight in +5:30, but in +6:00 it corresponds to 00:30 local, so it does not represent the invitee’s full local day. This makes the test’s stated intent (different timezone/day boundary behavior) potentially incomplete/misaligned, but it’s a test coverage/validity issue rather than a verifiable production defect from the diff.
